title: A mutex around half an update
shortDescription: Reason about a split critical section without invoking undefined behavior.
constraints: Ordinary C integer counter, initially zero. local is thread-local. Each lock/unlock pair forms a critical section. No other code accesses counter. Reason over all interleavings preserving each thread’s program order.
objectives: Distinguish a data race from a lost update
provenance: BitForge implementation example authored with Codex

options.rationale: This would require the read-modify-write sequence to be one critical section.
Both reads can observe zero, losing an update; alternatively one thread completes before the other reads.
Both threads eventually write a local value of at least one, so zero cannot be final.

options.text: Undefined behavior due to a data race
options.rationale: All shared counter accesses are protected by the same mutex. The compound operation is not atomic, but there is no unprotected conflicting counter access.

independent.source:
import json
final=set()
def explore(pc,local,counter):
 if pc==[2,2]:
  final.add(counter);return
 for t in range(2):
  if pc[t]==2:continue
  nextpc=pc.copy();nextlocal=local.copy();nextcounter=counter
  if pc[t]==0:nextlocal[t]=counter+1
  else:nextcounter=local[t]
  nextpc[t]+=1
  explore(nextpc,nextlocal,nextcounter)
explore([0,0],[0,0],0)
choices={"A":{2},"B":{1,2},"C":{0,1,2}}
print(json.dumps(next(k for k,v in choices.items() if v==final)))

explanation: The result is 1 or 2. If both threads read zero before either write, both later write one. If one completes before the other reads, the second writes two. Mutexes protect every shared access, so this is a lost-update logic error rather than a C data race. Hold the mutex across the entire increment to guarantee two.
reviewNotes: The verifier exhaustively enumerates the read and write critical sections in per-thread order. Local arithmetic can be folded into the read transition because local has no shared effects. Theoretical review separately checks that every counter access is mutex-protected.
